govdocs-archive_org-UAP_Encounters_Relea: FBI File 62-HQ-83894, Serials 246–301 — UAP Encounters Release 01 — gathers Bureau papers on UFO encounters. The declassified sheaf is a first-hand witness to G-man saucer-watching. The G-men took the reports seriously. The file is a primary source on official inquiry.
flying-for-france-with-the-american-esca: James McConnell — who would die in the war he describes — flew with the American Escadrille at Verdun and lived to tell it. His memoir of aerial combat is vivid, modest, and heartbreaking. A classic of aviation literature and a young hero's testament.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anastasius-gr: A 1913 entry on Anastasius Grün — the pen name of Count Auersperg, Austrian poet. Arthur Remy praises his verse. His Schutt sang of freedom. The empire heard his liberal song. A nobleman with a poet's heart. His Robin Hood sang the greenwood.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrew-of-wyn: This 1913 reference piece on Andrew of Wyntoun — the Scottish chronicler. Oswald Hunter-Blair praises his Orygynale Cronykil. His verse told Scotland's story. Macbeth lives in his lines. A prior with a poet's pen. His chronicle begins with Adam. His prior's cell overlooked the Firth.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-attila-the-hu: This 1913 reference article on Attila the Hun — the scourge of God. John Bertram Peterson tells his terrible march. St. Leo turned him from Rome. The Catalaunian fields broke his might. The barbarian who trembled before a pope. His empire died with its master.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-autun: A 1913 entry on Autun — the Burgundian diocese of the Roman town. Georges Goyau gives its ancient story. Its bishops date from the martyrs. The Janus temple guards its past. A see of the Morvan's edge. Its St. Lazare keeps the Romanesque portal.
